---
title: "Code quality"
---

The agent keeps slipping `print()` into production modules instead of using your logger, and bare `except:` clauses show up under deadline pressure. You want layered feedback. A fast advisory fires on every edit, a structural lint finds patterns regex cannot, a behavioral nudge reacts when the agent's narration repeats the antipattern, and a final LLM gate handles ambiguous cases.

<!-- gd-embed: code_quality.py -->

The same problem expressed at four escalating tiers, all firing on `Event.PostToolUse`. `hook(... Content(...))` runs a fast regex check on the edit, while `lint(...)` parses the file's AST so the bare-except check matches real handler nodes with line numbers, never a string or comment that merely mentions `except`. `nudge(... signals=...)` watches transcript narration to catch the agent talking about the antipattern, and `llm_gate(...)` lets a model adjudicate the ambiguous prod-print cases. Combine tiers when speed-vs-precision tradeoffs matter. See also [primitives](../guide/primitives.qmd) and [LLM hooks](../guide/llm-hooks.qmd) for the full set.
